newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar futures finish steadier.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar futures finish steadier.

text.p: LIFFE white sugar futures remained steadier during Wednesday evening trade, consolidating a recovery from recent declines, traders said.
Near December ended $0.80 a tonne higher at $328.00, while second month March finished at $329.00, up $1.00. Total volume was 2,448 lots.
Traders said the rally was not unexpected, as prices had been displaying oversold signals. There was also some offtake, with Tunisia buying 28,000 tonnes of whites for May/July delivery.
Traders said Wednesday's European Union (EU) white sugar tender had little market impact.
A total of 129,500 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 44.837 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos, according to the UK Intervention Board.
In Paris, December was $2.100 higher at $328.70, while March rose $2.40 to $330.00.
